What is your worst or weirdest experience with public transit?

The bus ride through SF's Chinatown at the time of day when school was letting out was at least the most memorable experience for me. There were us 2 white guys, and what seemed like at least 613 Asian children. Every stop more children got on. I don't know how they kept fitting, but they just kept increasing and increasing. It was very claustrophobic and amusing at the same time!

Just a few days ago I had a similar experience here in Spain. Except instead of Asian children on a bus, it was drunk Spanish teenagers (myself included) on a tram returning from an EDM festival. It was awesome.

Some transit employees came by (you know, the kind that see if you scanned your pass and fine you if you didn't pay), and I'm pretty sure nobody had scanned. However, they physically couldn't get on the tram, so we all got away with it :)

The first time I went to Germany, I got on the wrong bus in Frankfurt airport trying to get from the airport to the main train station. That bus took me about 30 minutes out, stopped at what looked to be a couple of factories, and then to what looked like a little remote village. It pulled up to a gas station and then everyone (including the driver) got off and just walked away.

This place was sketchy. Not like Oakland or bad-side of DC sketchy where you're likely to get mugged, but like some place you'd see in the movie Hostel. Never being to Germany before probably made it worse b/c it was my first point of comparison for Germany.

I spoke only a very small amount of German and I didn't have a European SIM so my phone didn't work. Luckily, I had gotten some Euros in the airport, so at least I had a little bit of money. I wandered around this town listening for anyone who may be speaking English only to recognize that most of the people weren't even speaking German so I was completely screwed. I ended up going into every gas station/7-11 shop I saw, buying a Coke, and trying to gauge whether the person working their spoke English.

About 2-hours after I'd gotten there and with it getting dark, I decided that I needed to just get out and try somewhere else. So I literally got on a 2nd random bus and just figured I'd try again where-ever it took me. Come to find out, that bus driver spoke English and helped me get back to the airport (where it turns out you can take a train directly to the main train station). Finally got to Frankfurt only to get chased by a crackhead through the streets....but that's a whole different story.

The rest of my trip was great and I've since been back a couple of times, but that first few hours in Germany was...well...weird. After meeting a bunch of Germans, I probably could've just walked up to one and straight-up asked how to get back to the airport, but at the time, I was a little creeped out by the whole Hostel-vibe.
Yup, you have to be careful with getting the right bus or train. You can literally end up in the bad part of town.
